Turn on \"Start head unit server\" in Android Auto’s developer settings

Android Auto closing the previous session

The dash stays black: force stop Android Auto
The connection to the dash dropped. REau comes back by itself; if it takes over a minute with the motorcycle on, turn it off and on with the key
Warns with sound and vibration when the dash or the phone needs something from you, such as turning the ignition off and on, or the phone being too hot
The dash is on but not accepting the connection. Turn the motorcycle’s ignition off and on again; REau reconnects by itself
The phone is hot (%1$d °C). Take it out of the sun or a closed pocket, or unplug the charger, so it does not slow down
Android is refusing the dash’s network
Android refused the dash’s Wi-Fi several times in a row. Turn off any VPN and the automatic switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data; if it goes on, turn the phone’s Wi-Fi off and on. REau keeps trying

resources.string: Trying to join the dash’s Wi-Fi
Android may ask to connect to the dash: tap Connect
Android Auto stopped sending pictures while you ride: the dash shows the last one
Android Auto in the browser, no dash
Turn off the other app’s streaming; REau tries again on its own
Letting go of Android Auto and the dash
Not enough free space on the phone to prepare the logs

Android Auto isn’t accepting the connection. Turn its head unit server on by hand: in Android Auto’s settings, tap \"Version\" about ten times to unlock developer settings, then, in the ⋮ menu, tap \"Start head unit server\". REau connects by itself as soon as it is on. The server turns off when the session ends (when you tap Turn off, for example), and after you restart the phone: turn it on again every time.
Android may pause REau while the screen is off to save battery. Exclude REau from battery optimization so the projection doesn’t drop.

Battery saver is on: with the screen off, Android cuts the network and location for background apps (the GPS card of the info ring can then be late). REau keeps going thanks to its pinned notification; if the dash or Android Auto drops, turn battery saver off.
Dash mask: darkens what doesn’t reach the dash’s round glass, using the fit chosen below, and shows where the dash ring is

Gemini by joystick: it listens through the helmet’s Bluetooth headset or, without one, the phone’s microphone. On by default, but the microphone stays closed until its permission is granted (Permissions shortcut). This switch is what makes the \"Gemini\" action on the Joystick page work, and a change applies the next time you turn on.
View only: touch here doesn’t reach Android Auto. The dash keeps receiving the picture normally.
Android Auto isn’t installed on this phone. Tap \"Get Android Auto\" to install it from Google Play, open it once to finish its setup, then come back.
Android Auto isn’t installed, and this phone has no app store or browser to get it from.
Couldn’t open Android Auto’s settings. Open Android Auto from your app list.
Open REau and type the full name in Bike data

The dash only accepts its full Wi-Fi name (for example RE_AB12_345678), and REau couldn’t find it: Android only lets apps scan for networks while REau is open on screen. Open \"Bike data\" and, in the \"Dash Wi-Fi\" group, type the full name in the \"Full Wi-Fi name\" field (if another dash is saved, tap \"Forget\" first); or turn on the projection with REau open.
Another app is using the dash (the phone’s port 2002 is busy): probably another dash app that’s streaming. Turn off its streaming; REau tries again on its own.

With the projection on, settings tagged LIVE apply right away, and so do the Weather switch, the joystick page, the network server screen and the Android Auto screen. Density applies too, but it restarts Android Auto and the picture freezes for a few seconds. Every other setting applies the next time you turn on.
From Android Auto: %1$s → on the dash: %2$s
the chosen part falls outside the Android Auto frame
the picture falls outside the dash frame
the picture would be too small
nothing would show on the glass

REau’s theme is the day and night signal it sends to Android Auto: Light and Dark fix it. By the sun: light from sunrise to sunset, dark at night, with the sun times from the phone’s position if \"Use location\" is on, or from the time zone (around 6 AM and 6 PM) if not. Waze and other apps follow only if their theme is set to automatic.

Android joins the dash’s Wi-Fi on its own when it appears, without the network picker and without REau having to look for the network. Android asks once whether you accept the network suggested by REau. Only works once the full dash name is known.
Record the video sent to the dash

Answer calls by joystick, in both dash modes: with the phone ringing, left answers and right or center declines; during a call, center hangs up. It also works for WhatsApp and other voice apps, through Android Auto. On by default, but it only acts once the phone permissions are granted (Permissions shortcut).
Detailed log: every dash packet and every Android Auto message in the log (much larger file; without the route card text). It only records while the diagnostic log is on.
Dash Wi-Fi \'%1$s\' not found nearby — check that it’s on and in range

The dash Wi-Fi \'%1$s\' is in range, but Android did not finish joining it (the phone may be slow to join with the screen off, the Android prompt may have been declined, or the password may be wrong). REau tries again by itself
Couldn’t connect to \'%1$s\' — network not found or wrong password

The dash Wi-Fi \'%1$s\' is refusing the connection. If the password is still the panel’s default one, the dash has frozen: turn the motorcycle off with the ignition key, wait about 30 seconds and turn it back on; REau keeps trying on its own
Android Auto is closing the previous session

Android Auto is still closing the previous session. It takes up to about 1 minute and REau tries again by itself. To skip the wait, in Android Auto’s settings, stop and start the head unit server again.

Android Auto is connected but isn’t sending a picture, and the dash stays black. Force stop it (Settings › Apps › Android Auto › Force stop), then turn REau off and on again. With Android Auto 17.4 or newer, also check that its head unit server is on.

Android Auto accepts the connection but doesn’t respond. In Android Auto’s developer settings, tap ⋮ and choose \"Stop head unit server\", then ⋮ and \"Start head unit server\"; REau tries again by itself.

The old REau app, the one with the seal on its icon, is still installed on this phone and may be using Android Auto: its head unit server takes only one session at a time. This app replaces it, so you can uninstall it. If it is on, turn it off (tap Turn off in it), wait about a minute and REau connects by itself.
Choose what each joystick tap does. Applies right away, even while the projection is on.
The dash shows the song that plays (music card): the media mode has a music control.
The dash does not show the song: put previous song, play/pause or next song on a media mode button.
The music card is off in Settings (Now playing).
What leaves the phone goes to the dash, to your network only with the network server on, and to the internet only for weather and updates (more in \"REau and your data\").
Special access (you turn these on yourself)
Up to you (Android asks, or you allow them in settings)
Without this, Android may pause REau with the screen off and the projection drops. It isn’t a permission: it’s the list of apps Android lets run in the background.
Shows the pinned projection notification with its Turn off button, asked when you turn on the projection (Android 13 or newer).
Answers and hangs up calls with the dash joystick, with the \"Answer calls\" switch on.
Tells REau whether the phone rings or is in a call, so the joystick acts at the right time, and the network generation (4G, 5G) for the dash, without reading numbers or calls.
Carries your voice from the helmet’s Bluetooth headset (or the phone) to Android Auto for Gemini, with the \"Gemini\" switch on, and REau doesn’t store the audio.
Lets REau find the dash in the Wi-Fi list behind another app; with \"Use location\", the position rounded to 11 km for sun and weather, and the GPS heading on the ring.
Android requires it for any connection, but REau uses the internet only for the optional weather (Open-Meteo) and, when you tap it, the update check (GitHub).
Know whether the dash Wi-Fi is connected and notice when it drops, to reconnect.
Find the dash network (the name starts with RE_) and check which Wi-Fi the phone is connected to.
Ask Android to connect to the dash Wi-Fi and, with automatic connection on, leave it as a suggested network.
Ask Android for the dash network, even without internet, and tie the dash connection to it; the rest of the phone stays on 4G.
The projection runs as a foreground service, with the pinned notification, so it keeps going with the screen off.
The service type Android has required for the projection since Android 14: the motorcycle’s dash is a connected device.
The same service with the location type: without it, behind another app or with the screen off, Android gives REau no Wi-Fi list and no GPS position.
The same service with the microphone type, only for Gemini by joystick: without it Android delivers silence with the screen off.
Keep the processor and Wi-Fi awake with the screen off while the projection is on; released when it turns off.
Choose the Bluetooth headset’s microphone for Gemini by joystick.
Lets REau show Android’s request to leave battery optimization, and on its own it changes nothing.
Added by an Android library (AndroidX) that REau uses, to protect the app’s internal notices, and it gives access to nothing on the phone.

Diagnostic log (on by default): records on the phone itself what happens in REau, to find bugs later; nothing leaves the phone unless you share it. When off, REau records nothing (neither the detailed log nor the copy of the system messages about REau), except the app’s crash report, which is written on the phone even then, stays only on the phone and never leaves by itself; what was already recorded stays until you delete it (or until the period set in \"Automatically delete\" ends)
Deletes all the logs stored on the phone and the last shared file. If the log is on, it starts again in a new file. This can’t be undone.
Deletes all the logs stored on the phone, the last shared file and the recordings of the video and of the Android Auto sessions. If the log is on, it starts again in a new file. This can’t be undone.
A local bridge between the phone’s Android Auto and the motorcycle’s dash: it adapts the picture, with music, caller and phone status, and sends it over the dash’s Wi-Fi.
To the dash, over its Wi-Fi: the picture and, with the default switches, music, caller and phone status; to the internet, only the optional weather and the update check when you tap.
The browser (only if you turn it on)
With \"Turn on the network server\" on (off by default), anyone on your network who enters the PIN sees the Android Auto picture, unencrypted, so don’t use it on strangers’ networks.
The diagnostic log has no position, streets, songs or caller; optional recordings (off by default) do; all stay on the phone, the crash report even with log off, and leave only through \"Share\".
What REau remembers about the dash
The dash’s Wi-Fi name and password and what it reported, encrypted with a key kept by Android, and the rounded position and last weather, if they exist, in the app’s folder.
Turn off the log and delete logs and recordings in Settings → Debug, and turn off the music and caller cards in Settings → On the dash.
What reaches Android Auto belongs to it: your voice in Gemini and Waze routes follow Google’s and Waze’s rules, not REau’s.

REau is an independent project, not affiliated with Royal Enfield or Google, and Royal Enfield, Tripper and the other names mentioned belong to their owners. It exists because these projects opened the way: tap one to copy its address.
Asks at once for the permissions Android prompts for; battery has its own button on its row. If Android doesn’t show the request (you declined before), use \"Open REau’s permissions in Android\".

On by default, but it only works once Android’s location permission is granted. With the theme set by the sun, REau reads the last position Android already has when you open it, without turning on GPS, to know sunrise and sunset where you are; rounded to about 11 km, it only leaves the phone for the weather service, never goes to the log, and is forgotten when this is off. That permission also lets REau see Wi-Fi networks to find the dash, even behind another app, without reading your position; Android may show the location icon.

Automatically deletes the log and recordings older than the chosen time (applies right away when you choose, and again when you open the app and with each new file). Past %1$d MB, the oldest logs go first whatever you choose; recordings have their own ceiling, %2$d MB.
Turn off by itself without the dash
If the dash stays gone this long (the bike switched off and forgotten), the projection stops and a notification says so
The projection keeps asking for the dash until you turn it off: that keeps the phone busy and drains the battery

When the dash’s Wi-Fi goes away and does not come back (the bike was switched off), REau keeps asking for it, with Android Auto, the video and the phone’s locks held, until you tap Turn off. With this on, the projection turns itself off after the time chosen without the dash, as the Turn off button would, and a notification says why. The count starts again whenever the dash comes back; \"No limit\" keeps the old behavior.
Showing the end of the file; the beginning was left out (in KB: %1$d). The whole file leaves through \"Share the logs\".
Tap Turn on before you ride
Letting go of Android Auto and the dash; you can turn it on again in a moment
Waiting for Android Auto and the dash
Not looking for the dash: open the address in the browser
The head unit server is missing
It takes up to a minute; REau tries again on its own
Stop and start its server in the ⋮ menu; REau tries again on its own
The dash shows the last picture while the bike moves
The dash is black: force stop Android Auto
The connection to the dash dropped. REau comes back by itself when it answers again. If the motorcycle is on and it takes over a minute, turn it off and on with the key
The dash stopped answering %1$d s ago. REau comes back by itself when it answers again. If the motorcycle is on and it takes over a minute, turn it off and on with the key
This disconnects the dash now and REau will ask for Android’s approval again. The projection is switched off first.
REau keeps trying to join the dash’s Wi-Fi
Android may ask whether REau can connect to the dash: tap Connect
Turn off the other app’s streaming
Location is off on the phone

With Android’s Location switched off, the phone does not return the Wi-Fi scan, so REau can’t see the dash’s network and may take longer to join it; the GPS card of the info ring and the theme by the sun don’t work either. Turn Location on in Android’s quick settings.
Android plays the “Dash alerts” channel without sound or vibration, so a stuck dash, a refused network or a hot phone would not be heard. Open its settings and give it sound.
Android blocks REau’s alerts (all notifications, or the “Dash alerts” channel), so a stuck dash, a refused network or a hot phone would not be warned. Open the settings and allow them.
A VPN is holding REau back
With REau inside the VPN, Android won’t let it use the dash’s Wi-Fi. In the VPN app, leave REau out (\"split tunneling\") and fully reconnect the VPN.
Applies right away with the projection on. The rest applies the next time you turn on.
Experimental: a 2 ms pause every 4 video packets, at most 400 a second
Mark Wi-Fi priority on debug builds
Experimental: only changes the debug build (a release always marks). Counts from the next connection
Experimental: aims at 200 kbps and follows what the encoder really puts out

Experimental: 5 more tries on the same network when Android refuses to bind to the dash (EPERM). The low-latency Wi-Fi lock left this switch: on Android 14 or later it changed nothing, and the choice of whoever had it on is kept. Counts from the next connection
Experimental: if the video encoder takes frames in and gives none out for 3 s, it is rebuilt (up to 3 times per stream)
Longer pause when asking for a keyframe
Experimental: when the picture breaks and a keyframe is asked of Android Auto, the video focus comes back after 400 ms instead of 100 ms. Counts from the next request
Ask for the dash on 2.4 GHz only
Experimental: the request for the dash\'s Wi-Fi names the 2.4 GHz band (Android 12 or later). A request that is not answered is asked once without the band. Counts from the next request
Experimental: if the app dies within 10 s of a start made with experimental switches on, they are switched off the next time the app opens, and the log says so
Experimental: with the map theme by the sun, the night theme lasts until sunrise instead of ending about half an hour before it. Counts from the next look, within a minute
Experimental: the weather is no longer sent to the dash once it was fetched more than 30 minutes ago (today, 3 hours). The dash has no room to tell the age of the data. Counts right away

Experimental: from 44 °C on the battery the video\'s top pace comes down (75, 62 and 50 percent of it, at 44, 46 and 48 °C) and goes back up only 3 °C under each step. For a phone whose Android thermal status never moves. Counts right away

Experimental: the speed profile reads the GPS speed when a route runs and the GPS is already on for the info ring (with “Use location” on); otherwise the route\'s estimate, as before. It never switches the GPS on. Counts right away
Experimental: a short “inactive” of Android Auto during a route (up to 8 s) shows on the dash as recalculating instead of clearing the route. Counts right away
Experimental: the dash\'s encoder is asked for BT.601, limited range, SDR. If the codec refuses, it is asked as before, and the log says what it accepted. Counts from the next video

Experimental: the handshake asks for protocol version 6.0 (today, 1.7). If Android Auto refuses it or the handshake fails, 1.7 is asked again until the app closes, and the log says what was asked and answered. Counts from the next time you turn on

Experimental: the dash\'s silence only goes to the log at 12 s and ends the session at 60 s (today, 4 s); when the dash is back, a keyframe is asked. Control packets leave 12 ms apart. Counts from the next connection

This is the dash whose full Wi-Fi name REau already knows, which it needs to connect. \"Forget\" deletes that name, everything the dash has reported (the bike data below) and the network suggested to Android; after that, REau looks for the dash again (with REau open, the name shows up on its own) or you type the full name. Use it when you change motorcycle or dash.

REau doesn’t know your dash’s full Wi-Fi name yet, and without it the dash won’t accept the connection. To find it automatically, Android requires the location permission: REau uses it only to see the list of Wi-Fi networks, never your position. Or type the full name below. If there is more than one dash nearby, check the name and use Forget.
Looking for the dash’s Wi-Fi… Turn on the motorcycle near the phone, with REau open: the name will appear here on its own.
Allow location (only to find the Wi-Fi)
As it appears in the phone’s Wi-Fi list, for example RE_AB12_345678
Your position, for the sun-based theme
Light by day, dark at night, by the sun
Title, album and artist on the dash

Shows the song’s title, album and artist on the dash’s music card, on by default; a change counts from the next time you turn on. The data comes from Android Auto, so no notification or contacts access is asked. The card only shows if a media-mode joystick button has previous song, play/pause or next song, which the standard page lacks: add one on the Joystick page.
Caller’s name (or number) on the dash

REau uses two fixed video profiles for the dash: A, %1$d fps and %2$d kbps, the smoother picture, and B, half of that (%3$d fps and %4$d kbps), lighter on the Wi-Fi and the dash. The maneuver profile and the speed profile, just below, choose between them. These values can’t be changed.
Profile A: 400 kbps. Profile B: %1$d kbps. Fixed

Picks the video profile by the distance to the route’s next maneuver: within 1 km of it, A; farther away, B, once the distance has changed by about 200 m (so it doesn’t keep switching). It only decides while a route is active. If the speed profile asks for B, B wins.

Picks the video profile by the route’s speed: up to about 55 km/h, A; from about 65 km/h, B; in between it stays as it was. It only decides while a route is active. If the maneuver profile asks for B, B wins.

The wallpaper is a still picture the dash shows in place of Android Auto, started by the \"Send wallpaper\" button on the home screen; it shows whole, unstretched and centered, with black around it (the ideal size is 526 × 300). REau keeps only the picture’s address, not a copy: if you delete or move the file, the dash shows a REau test card, and \"Reset to default\" goes back to the test picture. A change applies the next time the wallpaper starts.
FPS and bitrate on the video

Draws the frames per second and the bitrate of the last 5 s over the dash video, in red with a black outline (such as \"3.8 fps 187 kbps\"). When on, the position (X and Y) and the text size appear here. For testing and only in the debug build: it applies right away with the projection on, and the text sits over the map.
FPS and bitrate on the video

Draws the code of the last button the dash sent (such as \"0x05 PlayPause\") and, smaller, what REau did with it, over the dash video in orange with a black outline. The text stays until another button is pressed; when on, the position (X and Y) and the size appear here. For testing and only in the debug build: it applies right away and sits over the map.
Rain, wind, UV, air and sun, over the map

Draws a ring on the right of the dash’s picture, where the dash draws nothing, with one thing at a time that matters on the road: the weather (rain, wind, storms, UV, air quality, sun, temperatures) and the phone’s battery, signal and GPS. The dash’s down button in map mode shows and hides it; a dashed outline means an old forecast. It asks Open-Meteo for the weather every 15 minutes, from the rounded place of \"Use location\"; off, nothing is asked or kept, unless \"Weather on the dash\" is on.
Needs \"Use location\" on (Settings \u2192 Theme) and an internet connection on the phone.
On the left, where the dash draws the maneuvers. The two take turns

With the info ring on, the dash’s down button in map mode (on the joystick screen it can be given another action) shows the ring and hides it again, without touching the maneuver ring, which keeps its own rules. On (ring on the left, in the maneuver ring’s place), the info ring shows instead of the maneuver ring, so use it with that one off. The info ring goes away on the app menu and in other apps, and the choice is kept for next time.
Nothing is ticked: the ring stays off the video.

The rain falling now (and until when) or starting in the next hour (in how many minutes); it counts from 0.1 mm per 15 min, and above 7.6 mm/h the icon is heavy rain. Rain within 30 min goes ahead of the other data. Outside North America and Central Europe the forecast is hourly, so the minutes are rounded to 10 and marked with ~.
The strongest gust from now to 1 hour ahead. Shows from 40 km/h (caution, yellow); 55 is alert (orange); 70 is danger (red) and goes ahead of everything.
A thunderstorm now or in the next hour, from the forecast’s weather code. Always danger: the disk turns red and goes ahead of everything.
The UV index of the current hour. Shows only from 6 (high, orange); 8 is very high (red); 11 or more is extreme (violet).

The US air quality index (AQI). Shows only above 100: up to 150 is unhealthy for sensitive people (orange), up to 200 unhealthy (red), up to 300 very unhealthy (violet), above that hazardous (maroon).
The time to sunset or sunrise. Shows only when an hour or less is left.
The sky now in one word (clear, clouds, cloudy, fog, rain, snow) or \"dry\" when no rain is due in the next hour. Low priority: it shows when nothing more urgent is there.
Today’s high and low (such as 28/19°). Low priority.

The phone’s charge as a big number, with \"charging\", \"saver\" or \"on battery\". The colour follows the charge: green from 50 up, amber above 20, orange above 10, red below (percent). Not charging, 20 or less is caution; 10 or less is alert and goes ahead.

The network the phone carries data on: generation (5G, 4G…) and carrier, Wi-Fi, Starlink, satellite, airplane mode or no network. Bars go from green (3 to 4) to red (1). Airplane mode and no network are caution.

The GPS signal in 4 bars, from the position error: up to 5 m, 4 bars; up to 12 m, 3; up to 25 m, 2; worse, 1. No satellite is 0 bars and caution. The heading (compass point) shows only at 3.6 km/h or more.
Turns to the next data every few seconds. Off, it stays on the most urgent one
Another device opens the address in a browser

With the projection running, REau opens a server on the local network: a computer or car display with a browser, on the same network, opens the address, enters the 4-digit PIN and sees Android Auto. When on, REau doesn’t look for the dash; the PIN changes every time, and after 5 wrong attempts the device waits 5 minutes. The picture is sent unencrypted, to two browsers at most, and the server turns itself off when the projection ends.
Without this, the browser can only watch
With the switch on, the browser can also tap the Android Auto screen: open apps, make and answer calls, change the route. Turn it on only on a network you trust.

Phone: sound stays on the phone only (Waze’s voice goes to the helmet headset); Browser: sound goes only to the browser and the phone is silent (with \"Turn on the network server\" off, the phone plays); Both: both play. Switching between Phone and the other options restarts Android Auto for a moment. The browser only plays after a tap on the page.
The address and PIN appear in a moment, once the server is on.
This phone isn’t on any local network right now. Connect to a Wi-Fi network to get an address.
Anyone with this address and the PIN, on the same network, can see the Android Auto screen (map, route, who’s calling).

Keeps on the phone a copy of the video sent to the dash, with the map, the route and the cards it shows, to investigate picture problems. It is off by default in the app you install to ride and on in the debug build; it stays in the app’s folder and only leaves if you use \"Share › With recordings\". Recordings add up to 200 MB (1024 MB in the debug build), the oldest going first, and also go by the period in \"Automatically delete those older than\"; applies the next time you turn on.
Saves the map and the route

Records everything Android Auto sends in one connection (picture, route, music, caller, messages), keeping the last 50 to 100 MB, 3 to 15 minutes of ride (768 MB in the debug build). Off by default in the app you install to ride and on in the debug build, it reveals where you rode: it stays in the app’s folder and only leaves if you use \"Share › With recordings\". Recordings add up to 200 MB (1024 MB in the debug build) and go by the period in \"Automatically delete those older than\"; applies the next time you turn on.
Careful: the recordings contain the map, that is, where you rode, and the names of who calls. They stay on the phone.
Leaves the phone only when you tap here
Careful: “With recordings” sends out the map (where you rode) and the names of who calls. Share it only with someone you trust.
Right away, when the app opens and with each new file
Cap: %1$d MB of logs and %2$d MB of recordings
Tap and drag on the picture to use Android Auto.
Larger = bigger text and buttons. One value for the menu and the apps; changing it restarts the session.

Whole image: Android Auto’s picture fits inside the dash area, so the round edge hides no part of it. Center crop: takes only a middle part and enlarges it as far as the dash allows, with the crop’s size and place set below. The Mask, at the top, darkens what doesn’t reach the glass and shows where the dash ring is; applies right away.
In map mode, the up arrow is the dash’s own back button: it asks whether you want to exit navigation. REau sends no action for it.

In map mode, the down arrow shows and hides the info ring when it is on in the settings; it does not touch the maneuver ring. With the maneuver ring hidden, the dash stops sending this button, so no action comes out of it. With another action on this button, the ring is no longer switched by it.
In map mode, the center button puts the dash in media control. It can’t be changed.
During calls the buttons are fixed and the same in both dash modes: here you can only see what each one does. Needs the \"Answer calls\" switch.
The dash doesn’t send this tap
Applies to carrier calls and to WhatsApp and other voice apps.
If the helmet intercom answers first (after about 7.5 s of ringing), this tap hangs up the call that was already answered. While ringing, center doesn’t play or pause the music.
Applies to carrier calls and WhatsApp. After it acts, the same button is ignored for 3 s, so an accidental repeat tap does nothing.
One step per tap; the helmet follows.
While ringing, up and down stay as they are in the mode the dash is in (Map mode or Media control).
During a call the dash keeps left and right for itself: REau doesn’t receive those taps.
Uses the internet only for weather (on the dash or in the info ring), once the location is allowed, and to check for a new version when you tap.
Sends data only to your motorcycle’s dash (and, if you turn on the network server, to your local network).
The log stays on the phone, without your location.
REau is free software under the AGPL-3.0. Its source code is published here: tap to copy the address.
Signal, battery and GPS on the dash

Sends the dash the phone’s real status: the battery (and whether it’s charging), whether GPS is on and whether there’s network signal. When off, the dash always shows the same fixed values (battery at 62 percent, not charging, GPS on, signal present), which say nothing about the phone. Applies right away.
The image on the music card
Sends the album art to the dash’s music card (a small image, 75 by 75). It only shows with \"Now playing\" on and a song playing. Applies right away (the art shows at the next song or card update).
Off, the ring goes away and the dash looks cleaner

The dash’s own ring that shows the turn, off by default so the dash looks cleaner. Off, REau hides it everywhere except Waze and Google Maps, and while it is hidden the dash sends no map-mode joystick buttons: no zoom, and the down button cannot show or hide the info ring. The middle button (in Waze or Google Maps), the Android Auto screen or a call brings the ring back; applies right away.

When the dash last told REau something. Everything here comes from the dash; REau only shows it and never changes anything on it. \"Not reported yet\" means the dash has not sent that item: REau asks on connecting and every 15 minutes, and forgetting the dash clears it all.
On (the dash asks for an update)

How far the bike can still go on its fuel, as the dash counts it: REau only shows the number the dash sends (about every 5 seconds), converted if the dash is in miles, and never changes anything on it. It falls as you ride and rises when you refuel; with the bike off or the dash out of reach, it shows the last value and the line below tells when. The fuel pump before the number is the dash’s low-fuel warning: it blinks yellow while on.
Temperature and weather icon, over the internet

When on, REau asks the Open-Meteo service when you open REau and every 15 minutes, and sends the dash the current temperature and an icon (sun, cloudy, rain, storm or snow); off, the dash gets none and the stored weather is deleted. It needs \"Use location\" on and internet; with no internet the last weather is used for up to 3 hours. The temperature in the dash’s top bar still comes from the bike’s own thermometer; what you see here is the weather service’s.
